newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan institutions to boost stock holdings.
newsitem.headline: Japan institutions to boost stock holdings.

text.p: Institutional investors in Japan are planning to boost their stock holdings in October, continuing a trend from the previous month, a Reuters investment survey showed on Monday.
The survey showed that a view was gaining ground among investors that both stock and bond markets would remain stable in the month ahead.
The monthly Global Asset Allocation survey asked 17 Japan-based financial institutions about their recommended investment strategy in October.
The average overall portfolio weighting of equities rose to 47.67 percent, up 0.42 of a percentage point from the previous survey for September.
The Japanese investors surveyed are increasing their investment in U.S. and French stocks.
The average weighting of U.S. stocks in October rose to 35.09 percent, marking the highest average weighting since June 1994.
At the same time, the institutions are cutting back their investment in British, German and domestic stocks, it showed.
The average overall weighting for bond investments, meanwhile, stood at 36.67 percent, unchanged from the previous month.
Japanese investors are increasing their investment in U.S., French, German and Asian bonds.
They are scaling back their investment in Japanese, Canadian and other European bonds.
The average weighting for Japanese bonds fell 0.88 point from the previous survey to 15.81 percent, down from the previous record low of 15.92 percent marked in July 1996.
The survey showed cash investments in October fell to 15.67 percent, down 0.41 point from the previous survey, the lowest level since March 1995.
